@ARTICLE{Gershman2022-sk,
title = "The molecular memory code and synaptic plasticity: a
synthesis",
author = "Gershman, Samuel J",
abstract = "The most widely accepted view of memory in the brain holds
that synapses are the storage sites of memory, and that
memories are formed through associative modification of
synapses. This view has been challenged on conceptual and
empirical grounds. As an alternative, it has been proposed
that molecules within the cell body are the storage sites of
memory, and that memories are formed through biochemical
operations on these molecules. This paper proposes a
synthesis of these two views, grounded in a computational
theory of memory. Synapses are conceived as storage sites
for the parameters of an approximate posterior probability
distribution over latent causes. Intracellular molecules are
conceived as storage sites for the parameters of a
generative model. The theory stipulates how these two
components work together as part of an integrated algorithm
for learning and inference.",
journal = ArXiv,
